rules: Every headline number is resolved at build time from the cited source file: 'path' is a JSON path inside a JSON file; 'text' must occur verbatim in a Markdown/CSV file. A number that cannot be resolved makes the build fail; it is never typed in by hand.

Status labels follow the files' own wording. 'completed_screen_failed' means the run finished and its prespecified screen failed. 'unavailable_here' means the evidence is not present on this machine and nothing about it is verified here.

Era labels: unifloral_titan and unifloral_zeus use the pinned Unifloral TD3+BC host (td3_bc.py sha256 6f5ab6f9...). corl_host pages use the repository's earlier CORL-derived host and are archived, not part of this interface's evidence.

experiments.title: Unifloral TD3+BC parity validation

experiments.plain: Software check. The hash-checked Unifloral TD3+BC definitions and the one-critic-per-call candidate that the later experiments drive produce identical states, so what follows runs on the real Unifloral host.

experiments.title: BCA pipeline validation on the Unifloral host (19 checks)
experiments.question: Do the auxiliary fit, the calibration refresh, the frozen reference and the actor-side penalty behave as specified, and does kappa = 0 reproduce the host bit for bit?

headline.label: Same gradient with the freeze removed
Test-snapshot threshold R (manual early refresh, 128 scores)

experiments.plain: Software check on a fresh snapshot, not an efficacy result. It establishes that the penalty enters only the actor objective, that the action gradient through the width is live while the reference is frozen, and that resume is byte exact.

experiments.title: The 20,000-update Unifloral checkpoint (kappa 0, live auxiliary fits)
experiments.question: Train one native Unifloral TD3+BC actor-critic on the recorded data while fitting and calibrating BCA's auxiliary model alongside, with no penalty applied.
experiments.plain: The one trained model every later diagnostic and pilot starts from. Its first export was blocked by a seed-domain check and recovered exactly on the same day. Its own calibration threshold at update 20,000 is inside the runtime assets and is not shown here.

experiments.title: Frozen-checkpoint decision diagnostic, development batch 1 (64 states)
experiments.question: On a fixed bank of nine candidate actions per state, does Q1 - kappa U pick higher simulator-reference actions than raw Q1, the actor's own action or simple controls?

headline.label: Q1 - 3U mean paired gain over raw Q1
Actor's own action, gain over raw Q1
Mean signed Q1 error (Q1 - V) over 576 candidates

experiments.plain: A forced-probe diagnostic: candidates are imposed, not chosen by a policy. The pointwise interval for every penalty strength includes zero. Decision advantage was not established.

experiments.title: Frozen-checkpoint strength comparison, development batch 2 (64 states)
experiments.question: Same question on 64 new development starts, with contrast-matched actor-distance and head-disagreement controls across seven strengths.

headline.label: Q1 - 3U mean paired gain over raw Q1
Contrast-matched actor-distance control (kappa 0.1), gain over raw Q1
Mean signed Q1 error (Q1 - V) over 576 candidates

experiments.plain: The checkpoint overestimates most candidates by a wide margin. Penalizing with 3U moves a handful of choices; a cheap actor-distance control at strength 0.1 gains about as much. No strength was selected.

experiments.title: Saved-bank mechanism audit: does the width point toward the better action?
experiments.question: Among states where raw Q1 picked a worse candidate, does a larger width sit on the worse action (supporting the switch) or on the better one (opposing it)?

headline.label: Batch 1: states where raw Q1 had positive regret
Batch 1: width supports the better candidate
Batch 1: width opposes the better candidate
Batch 2: states where raw Q1 had positive regret
Batch 2: width supports the better candidate
Batch 2: width opposes the better candidate
Overall: states where raw Q1 had positive regret
Overall: width supports the better candidate
Overall: width opposes the better candidate
Within-state Pearson, U versus signed Q1 error
Within-state Pearson, U versus candidate-bank regret
Pairwise sign agreement of U with the signed-error contrast (0.5 = chance)

experiments.plain: Descriptive direction evidence on the saved banks. The sign of the width contrast between the raw pick and the better candidate is what a correction would need; here it more often points the wrong way.

experiments.title: Grouped width validation: does the width add held-out predictive information?
experiments.question: With all candidates of an episode grouped into one fold, does adding the training-residualized width to a base predictor of the Q1-minus-V discrepancy lower held-out error, compared with a permuted-width control?

headline.label: Held-out MSE reduction from adding the width (8-fold, grouped by episode)
Same for a within-episode permuted width (negative control)
Held-out MSE, base plus residual width
Pairwise ranking score change, width minus base

experiments.plain: The width carries some information about where Q1 is off, beyond a base predictor, and a shuffled width carries none. This is predictive association, not a decision result.

experiments.title: Decision utility of the width's predictive information (out-of-fold)
experiments.question: If the out-of-fold corrected scores are used to choose candidates, does the one that uses the width choose better than the one that does not?

headline.label: Mean paired gain, corrected-with-width minus corrected-without
Episodes where the two corrected scores disagree (of 128)
Mean selected V, original BCA kappa 3 (reference row)
Mean selected V, corrected with width

experiments.plain: The interval of the primary gain includes zero and the disagreements split almost evenly. Predictive association did not turn into better choices on these banks.

experiments.title: Scale and gradient audit of the width against Q1 on the fitting bank
experiments.question: How large is the width's variation across candidate actions compared with Q1's, and how much of the actor gradient does the penalty supply at kappa 1?

headline.label: Action-centered RMS contrast of Q1 across candidates
Action-centered RMS contrast of U across candidates
Penalty-to-Q actor-gradient norm ratio at kappa 1, raw U (32 rows)
Gradient through the frozen reference / through the live action

experiments.plain: The width is about 5 Q-units high but varies by only about 0.15 across a state's candidates, thirty times less than Q1 itself varies; at kappa 1 its gradient is about 4% of Q1's. That is why small strengths change nothing and large ones act like a constant shift.

experiments.title: Frozen operator-alignment audit and its Zeus analysis
experiments.question: Within a state's nine candidates, does the width track its own native residual, and does that residual track the signed Q1 error against the simulator?

headline.label: Within-state corr(|native residual|, signed Q1 error)
Residual containment |R| <= U on the development bank

experiments.plain: High containment coexists with almost no within-state discrimination between actions. The band covers its own residual but does not rank candidates by their true error.

experiments.title: Cached target/action-scoring comparison (privileged controls)
experiments.question: On the same 128-state bank, do fixed control scores that use evaluator-derived information pick better actions than Q1?

headline.label: Mean-native-target selector, gain over Q1, batch 1
Mean-native-target selector, gain over Q1, batch 2

experiments.plain: A privileged control, not a deployable method: it needs the evaluator's reward and next state. It shows that better choices exist in these banks, so a test on them is not vacuous.

experiments.title: Lower-only ideal-penalty feasibility (privileged control)
experiments.question: Can lowering scores alone, never raising them, improve choices on these banks?
experiments.plain: Feasibility only: a penalty that only subtracts can help here if it subtracts the right amounts. Whether a learned, calibrated width can do that is the open question.

Stream 1: BCA gain over native continuation

Stream 1: BCA gain over distance control

experiments.plain: The one positive policy-return result. Two continuation streams from a single trained checkpoint on 32 shared nominal starts, so it is not independent-seed evidence and not an out-of-distribution test.

This did not establish adaptivity or underestimation detection. Folders bca_adaptive_signal_screen_v1 and bca_adaptive_signal_recovery_v1 are not present on this machine.

experiments.title: Direct held-out BCA evaluation, 64 action banks (reported)
experiments.question: On 32 shared held-out starting states and two checkpoints, does original BCA fix raw Q1's wrong choices?
experiments.reported: Reported by the user: 64 action banks; raw Q selected a suboptimal candidate in 25 banks; BCA changed three choices, one improved and two worsened; decision advantage over raw Q and controls was not established; the fixed detection check was inconclusive because error-class coverage was insufficient; among the 25 wrong-choice banks the penalty contrast favored the better action in nine and pointed the wrong way in sixteen. Descriptive findings, not a tuning dataset. Folder not present on this machine.
experiments.plain: Unavailable on this machine.
